text:
elaine: heads-up, after the continuous-batcher rollout yesterday we're seeing an unexpected drop in prompt-fragment cache hit-rate for several high-qps models. noticed during the 02:00 deploy window.

mike: saw this on the dashboards too. hit-rate went from ~82% -> ~66% on prod for model:gptx-derive. latency p75 bumped ~15ms.

raj: do we have a quick profile? is it cache key churn or batch composition?

elaine: short profile attached (small sample):
```
batcher: continuous v2.4.1
workload: mixed short/long prompts
cache_hits: 66
cache_misses: 34
median_batch_size: 6
unique_prefixes_per_batch: 5.2
cohort_entropy: high
```

sam: that entropy number stands out. continuous batching is coalescing requests by arrival window rather than prefix affinity, so batches are more heterogeneous -> fewer shared prefix prefixes in each batch -> worse prefix reuse in the KV cache.

jess: can we route by prefix-hash mod N to keep similar prefixes together? tradeoff is increased queueing latency for small tail requests.

mike: exactly. right now we favor latency SLOs so we flush at 8ms. grouping by prefix increases wait time. we need to quantify latency vs hit-rate delta.

elaine: quick AB we ran:
- control (continuous v2.3 flush=8ms): hit=82%, p75=78ms
- roll (v2.4 flush=8ms no-affinity): hit=66%, p75=93ms
- affinity-mode (v2.4 flush=12ms with prefix-hash grouping): hit=80%, p75=98ms
so affinity recovered hits but p75 higher.

raj: numbers useful. the ~5-6ms extra queueing vs ~15ms p75 delta suggests some other factor too (kernel selection or kv lookup path). any CPU spikes?

sam: we saw CPU on the KV proxy jump ~12% when misses rose. cache miss -> full KV deserialization + kernel warm path.

jess: is kernel selection changing because batch composition changes sequence length distribution? more diverse prefixes -> wider seq len range -> different kernel choices -> less efficient. need a trace.

build-bot: deploy 1955554000 -> continuous-batcher v2.4.1 rolled to 80% of serving nodes at 1955554100.

elaine: plan proposals:
1) short-term: enable soft-affinity heuristic: prefer prefix-key grouping within a 5ms window, keep flush at 8ms. should improve reuse with small latency hit. can canary to 10% traffic.
2) medium-term: implement adaptive flush threshold based on recent cohort entropy and target hit-rate. if entropy high, increase window. if low, shrink.
3) long-term: add prefetch/warmup for top-K prefixes (hot cohorts) when their request rate spikes.

mike: +1 for soft-affinity canary. also we should instrument per-batch 'distinct_prefix_fraction' metric.

raj: I'll add a profiler run to capture kernel selection breakdown across batch compositions. can compare kernel times for homogeneous vs heterogeneous batches.

jess: also a thought: KV keying might be sensitive to prompt normalization changes. any recent prompt-normalizer tweaks?

elaine: no changes to normalizer in this rollout. input parsing unchanged. root cause likely coalescing policy.

sam: temporary mitigation: reduce batcher concurrency on the hottest model for 1 hour to lower miss storm and CPU pressure. revert if we see latency regress.

mike: ok canary plan: soft-affinity to 10% for model:gptx-derive, add distinct_prefix_fraction and kernel-selection histogram. roll at 1955555400 if metrics look good.

jess: will set alert for hit-rate drop >5% or p75 increase >20ms during the canary.

elaine: thanks. I'll post follow-ups once the canary starts. :thumbsup:

sam: ping me when canary starts, I'll watch CPU/KV metrics. :eyes:

raj: starting profiler capture now (10s sampling) on two nodes and uploading the tar to /tmp/prof-195555.

elaine: great thread. saving notes here so we don't lose context.

mike: one more note — we should consider adding a small per-request 'cohort-id' header so routing can be cheaper rather than recomputing prefix-hash on every arrival.

jess: agreed. will add an RFC for cohort-id header after the canary.

build-bot: canary scheduled: 1955555400 -> 1955559000, target 10% traffic, rollback on alerts.

elaine: closing for now, will update with canary outcomes.
